source: Hand-written to AWS's own docs: S3 storage classes and their minimums (S3 pricing and user guide), Route 53 record types and routing policies (Route 53 developer guide), AWS WAF managed rule groups and rate-based rules (AWS WAF developer guide). Tiers: 1 first plays, 2 after a couple of plays, 3 for regulars.

fishing.name: profile-pic.jpg
fishing.hint: Shown on every page load
fishing.why: Read constantly → S3 Standard: no retrieval fees, millisecond access.

fishing.name: app-bundle.js
fishing.hint: Downloaded by every visitor
fishing.why: Hot data → Standard. Tip: put CloudFront in front of it.

fishing.name: thumbnail-42.png
fishing.hint: Loaded thousands of times a day
fishing.why: Frequent reads make Standard cheapest overall.

fishing.name: logo.svg
fishing.hint: On every page of the shop
fishing.why: Read all day → Standard (and cache it at the edge with CloudFront).

fishing.name: today-orders.csv
fishing.hint: Read by the dashboard every few minutes
fishing.why: Hot and changing → Standard.

fishing.name: tax-return-2015.pdf
fishing.hint: Must keep it, will never open it
fishing.why: Cold archive → Glacier (Deep Archive is even cheaper).

fishing.name: audit-logs-2019.zip
fishing.hint: Kept 7 years for compliance, never read
fishing.why: Archive → Glacier. For files kept years and never read, Glacier Deep Archive is cheapest, and waiting hours to restore is fine.

fishing.name: old-emails-2012.mbox
fishing.hint: Kept for legal reasons only
fishing.why: Kept but never read → an archive class: Glacier.

fishing.name: invoice-2023.pdf
fishing.hint: Opened about once a month
fishing.why: Infrequent but must open instantly → Standard-IA: cheaper storage, small fee per GB you read.

fishing.name: quarterly-report.xlsx
fishing.hint: Checked a few times per quarter
fishing.why: Warm data → Standard-IA: a lower storage price, plus a small fee per GB you read back.

fishing.name: db-backup.sql.gz
fishing.hint: Restored only in emergencies, needs to be quick
fishing.why: A backup that must restore fast → Standard-IA: millisecond reads, 30-day minimum. Glacier Instant Retrieval is also instant and cheaper to store, but bills at least 90 days per object.

fishing.name: raw-footage-2018.mov
fishing.hint: Old project, kept just in case
fishing.why: Rarely if ever touched → Glacier. Use a lifecycle rule to move it automatically.

fishing.name: dr-site-backup.tar
fishing.hint: Needed fast if the main site fails, otherwise untouched
fishing.why: Rarely read but must be ready in seconds → Standard-IA, not an archive that takes hours.

fishing.name: last-month-logs.gz
fishing.hint: Searched when something breaks, a few times a month
fishing.why: Read now and then, must open at once → Standard-IA.

fishing.name: course-video-week1.mp4
fishing.hint: Every new student watches it
fishing.why: Streamed constantly → Standard, with CloudFront in front.

fishing.name: research-dataset-2016.parquet
fishing.hint: Finished study, kept for reproducibility
fishing.why: Kept for years, rarely if ever read → Glacier.

fishing.name: monthly-statement-archive.zip
fishing.hint: Customers download last year's statements now and then
fishing.why: Occasional reads that must be instant → Standard-IA.

fishing.name: feature-flags.json
fishing.hint: Read by every server on start-up, many times an hour
fishing.why: Small and read all the time → Standard. Per-request fees matter more than storage here.

fishing.name: ct-scans-2010.dcm
fishing.hint: Hospital must keep them 15 years, almost never opened
fishing.why: Long retention, rare access, hours to restore is acceptable → Glacier (Deep Archive is cheapest).

fishing.name: photo-contest-entries-2022.zip
fishing.hint: Judged and finished; maybe reused in a yearbook
fishing.why: Done with, kept just in case → Glacier.

fishing.name: tiny-config-2kb.yml
fishing.hint: Opened once a month, only 2 KB
fishing.why: A trick: Standard-IA bills every object as at least 128 KB, so a tiny file can cost more there. Standard is cheaper for very small objects.

fishing.name: temp-upload-chunk.part
fishing.hint: Deleted within a day
fishing.why: Standard-IA bills 30 days minimum and Glacier 90, so short-lived files belong in Standard.

fishing.name: legal-hold-contract.pdf
fishing.hint: Never opened, but a lawyer might need it within minutes
fishing.why: Must be readable at once when needed → not an archive that takes hours. Standard-IA (or Glacier Instant Retrieval) fits.

fishing.name: user-avatar-inactive.png
fishing.hint: Belongs to an account nobody has used for two years
fishing.why: Cold, but the user might log in tomorrow and expect it instantly → Standard-IA.

fishing.name: nightly-build-artifact.tar
fishing.hint: Kept 7 days, then deleted
fishing.why: Deleted before 30 days → Standard; IA and Glacier charge minimum storage periods.

fishing.name: music-master-1999.wav
fishing.hint: Original recording, kept forever, restored maybe once a decade
fishing.why: The textbook archive → Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest place in S3.

fishing.name: game-patch-v2.1.bin
fishing.hint: Everyone downloads it this week, nobody after
fishing.why: Hot now → Standard; add a lifecycle rule to move it to Standard-IA later.

fishing.name: annual-report-2024.pdf
fishing.hint: Popular in March, quiet the rest of the year
fishing.why: Mostly quiet with bursts → Standard-IA works; S3 Intelligent-Tiering would move it for you automatically.

fishing.name: security-camera-week3.mp4
fishing.hint: Kept 90 days in case of an incident, rarely viewed
fishing.why: Kept a few months and must play at once if needed → Standard-IA.

fishing.name: compliance-ledger-2008.csv
fishing.hint: Regulator may ask, you can take a day to answer
fishing.why: Rare access with time to spare → Glacier is far cheaper to keep.

route53.q: Point www.example.com at the IPv4 address 203.0.113.10
route53.why: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address.

route53.q: Point api.example.com at an IPv6 address
route53.why: AAAA records hold IPv6 addresses.

route53.q: Route email for example.com to the mail servers
route53.why: MX records say which servers accept mail for a domain.

route53.q: Publish a plain-text verification string a service gave you
route53.why: TXT records hold any text you need, such as verification tokens.

route53.q: Make blog.example.com another name for myblog.host.net
route53.why: A CNAME points one name at another name. It can't sit at the zone apex.

route53.q: Send each user to whichever of your Regions gives them the lowest latency
route53.why: Latency-based routing sends users to the Region with the lowest latency for them.

route53.q: Serve a backup site only when the primary fails its health check
route53.why: Failover routing uses health checks to switch to a secondary.

route53.q: One web server, one address, nothing fancy
route53.why: Simple routing answers with the record's value. Fine for a single resource.

route53.q: Canary release: 90% of traffic to v1, 10% to v2
route53.why: Weighted routing splits traffic by the weights you assign.

route53.q: Show German users the German site based on where they are
route53.why: Geolocation routing answers based on the user's location (continent, country or US state).

route53.q: Point the zone apex example.com at a CloudFront distribution
route53.why: Route 53 alias records can point the apex at AWS resources like CloudFront. A CNAME can't sit at the apex.

route53.q: Point the apex at an Application Load Balancer
route53.why: Alias records point at load balancers by name and follow their changing addresses.

route53.q: Hand a subdomain over to another team's name servers
route53.why: NS records delegate a (sub)domain to the name servers that answer for it.

route53.q: Allow only Amazon's certificate authority to issue certificates for your domain
route53.why: CAA records list which certificate authorities may issue certificates for the domain.

route53.q: Look up which name belongs to an IP address (reverse DNS)
route53.why: PTR records map an IP address back to a name.

route53.q: Tell clients the host and port of your voice service
route53.why: SRV records give a service's host, port, priority and weight.

route53.q: Return up to eight healthy servers at random, each with a health check
route53.why: Multivalue answer routing returns several healthy records, a simple kind of load spreading.

route53.q: Names that only resolve inside your VPC
route53.why: A private hosted zone answers only for the VPCs you associate with it.

route53.q: Add the email-signing records Amazon SES gives you for your domain
route53.why: SES Easy DKIM gives you three CNAME records to publish.

route53.q: Say which servers may send email for your domain (SPF)
route53.why: SPF policies are published as TXT records.

route53.q: Moving to new servers tomorrow: what do you lower today so the switch spreads fast?
route53.why: A short time to live means resolvers re-ask sooner, so the new address takes over quickly.

route53.q: Route customers by which network (IP range) they come from
route53.why: IP-based routing answers by the client's IP address range (CIDR blocks you define).

route53.q: Send more users to a Region by growing its area on the map, with a bias
route53.why: Geoproximity routing uses where users and resources are, and a bias to grow or shrink a Region's share.

route53.q: Stop sending traffic to v2 without deleting its record
route53.why: A weighted record with weight 0 gets no traffic (unless every record is 0).

route53.q: Which DNS queries does Route 53 not charge for?
route53.why: Alias queries to AWS resources like CloudFront, ELB and S3 websites are free.

route53.q: A record created for you in every hosted zone, naming the main name server
route53.why: Each hosted zone gets an SOA (start of authority) record and NS records automatically.

route53.q: Failover only works if Route 53 can tell the primary is down. What does it need?
route53.why: Failover routing switches when the primary's health check fails.

route53.q: Users in a country you didn't list get which answer under geolocation routing?
route53.why: Without a default record, users from unlisted places get no answer, so add one.

route53.q: Send 100% to blue, then shift slowly to green with no new DNS names
route53.why: Change the weights step by step: a blue/green rollout.

route53.q: Keep the apex working when the CloudFront distribution's addresses change
route53.why: Alias records track the target's current addresses for you.
